name: Door-Anchored Band Row (chest height)
cues: Anchor at chest height, step back until the band is taut
Ribs down, squeeze the shoulder blades back and down before the elbows bend
Elbows brush the ribs; pause one second at the back
mistakes: Leaning back to finish the pull
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
regression: Lighter band or step closer to the door; seated on a chair
progression: Heavier band, 3-sec return, or single-arm anti-rotation row
setupCue: Anchor at chest height, band taut
youtube: E3 Rehab banded row door anchor
The Prehab Guys resistance band row
source: Horizontal pulling for scapular retractors; anchored band gives a fixed line of pull (clinical S&C consensus; Andersen et al. 2010 elastic vs dumbbell EMG similar).

name: High-Anchor Face Pull with External Rotation
cues: Anchor above head height, palms facing down
Pull toward your eyes and spread the band, thumbs finish pointing back
Chin tucked, ribs stacked over the pelvis
mistakes: Arching the low back to finish the pull
regression: Lighter band, or the plain band face pull without the anchor
progression: Half-kneeling or 2-sec hold at the back
source: Same pattern as the cable face pull; trains lower trapezius and external rotators for upper-crossed posture (Cools et al. 2007 scapular exercise selection).

name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
cues: Kneel side-on to the anchor, inside knee down, cushion under the knee
Squeeze the down-side glute so the hip is long, ribs down
Press straight out, hold, resist the turn
mistakes: Hips sagging back toward the heel
Letting the trunk rotate toward the anchor
regression: Standing Pallof (existing) with a lighter band
progression: Tall-kneeling Pallof, then Pallof with overhead press
youtube: E3 Rehab half kneeling pallof press
The Prehab Guys pallof press progression
source: Anti-rotation core endurance with no spinal motion (McGill 2015, Back Mechanic); half-kneeling removes leg drive and adds hip-flexor length on the down side.

name: Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press
cues: Both knees down, hips fully open, glutes squeezed
Ribs stacked over the pelvis, press straight out
Breathe out as you press and hold
mistakes: Arching the low back to stay upright
progression: Pallof with overhead press, or slower 10-sec holds
youtube: Squat University tall kneeling pallof press
source: Narrower base than half-kneeling, so higher demand on anti-rotation and hip extensors (clinical S&C progression consensus).

name: Pallof Press with Overhead Reach
cues: Press out first, then reach the hands up only as far as the ribs stay down
Exhale on the reach, glutes squeezed
Bring the hands back to the chest along the same path
mistakes: Ribs flaring and low back arching as the arms go up
regression: Half-kneeling Pallof press without the overhead reach
progression: Split stance standing, heavier band
youtube: The Prehab Guys pallof press with overhead reach
source: Adds an anti-extension challenge to anti-rotation; the reach stops where the ribs flare, so no lumbar arch (rule for extension-intolerant).

name: Tall-Kneeling Band Lat Pulldown
cues: Anchor at the top of the door, kneel facing it
Pull the elbows down to the ribs, chest stays proud but ribs stay down
Control the return for 2 seconds
mistakes: Leaning back and arching the low back
Shrugging as the arms go up
regression: Seated on a chair, lighter band
progression: Single-arm pulldown or heavier band
youtube: Jeff Cavaliere band lat pulldown door
source: Vertical pulling for lat and lower trap strength; tall-kneeling with glutes on keeps the pelvis neutral.

name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
cues: High anchor, arms long, slight soft elbows
Sweep the hands down to the thighs, ribs pulled down
Exhale fully at the bottom
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a row
Arching the back as the arms go up
progression: Tall-kneeling version, or 3-sec lowering
youtube: E3 Rehab band straight arm pulldown
source: Same movement as the cable straight-arm pulldown; lats plus an anti-extension trunk (exhale-ribs-down pattern).

name: Anchored-Band Dead Bug (anti-extension press)
cues: Lie with your head toward a low anchor, hold the band above your chest, arms straight
Pull the band toward your knees and keep it there, low back gently into the floor
Lower one leg slowly while the band tension stays
mistakes: Low back lifting off the floor as the leg lowers
Letting the arms drift back toward the anchor
regression: Existing dead bug, or keep the heel touching the floor
progression: Heavier band or straighter leg
youtube: E3 Rehab dead bug progressions band
The Prehab Guys dead bug pullover band
source: Banded pullover adds lat co-contraction to the anti-extension dead bug (common physio progression; McGill-informed neutral spine).

name: Door-Anchored Band Chest Press
cues: Back to the door, anchor at chest height, split stance
Press forward and slightly together, ribs down
Shoulder blades glide forward at the end
mistakes: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
progression: Single-arm press (adds anti-rotation)
youtube: The Prehab Guys serratus punch band
source: Pressing balance for a pull-heavy corrective plan; serratus anterior protraction at the end of range (Ludewig 2004).

name: Banded External Rotation at 90 Degrees
cues: Anchor at chest height, elbow at shoulder height and bent to a right angle
Rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling, elbow stays still
Slow 3-sec lower
mistakes: Arching the low back to get range
regression: External rotation with the elbow at your side and a towel roll
progression: Hold 3 sec at the top or heavier band
setupCue: Elbow up, bent at right angle
youtube: E3 Rehab external rotation 90 degrees band
source: Rotator cuff endurance in the overhead-ready position (Reinold et al. 2004 EMG).

name: Band Y-T-W Raises
cues: Anchor at chest height, stand tall, step back
Draw a Y, then a T, then a W with straight-ish arms, thumbs up
Blades slide down and back, chin tucked
mistakes: Leaning back or arching the low back
progression: Hold each letter 3 sec
youtube: The Prehab Guys band Y T W
source: Lower and middle trapezius emphasis; done standing so the low back never extends (prone YTW avoided for extension-intolerant).

name: Band Hip Hinge (RDL pattern)
cues: Stand on the band, hold the ends at your hips, soft knees
Push the hips back with a long neutral spine, band tension rises
Stand up by squeezing the glutes, stop tall, no lean back
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower
regression: Dowel hip hinge (existing hiphinge) with no band
progression: Heavier band, or single-leg supported hinge
setupCue: Stand on band, ends at hips
source: Hinge with a neutral spine loads hips not lumbar flexion; elastic gives most resistance at lockout where the glute is shortest. Finish tall, no hyperextension.

name: Band Split Squat
cues: Front foot on the band, ends at your shoulders, back heel up
Lower straight down, trunk tall, ribs over pelvis
Drive through the front heel and squeeze the back-leg glute
mistakes: Leaning back and arching at the bottom
regression: Bodyweight split squat holding a chair
progression: Heavier band, or 3-sec lowering
source: Unilateral leg strength with low spinal compression; back-leg glute squeeze lengthens the hip flexor (counter to APT).

name: Monster Walk (mini-band)
cues: Band above the knees, quarter squat, feet hip-width and pointing forward
Step diagonally forward, keep tension, knees out over toes
Pelvis level, no rocking
mistakes: Swaying the trunk side to side
progression: Band around the ankles or forefoot
source: Gluteus medius activation in a functional stance (Cambridge et al. 2012); feet kept straight to train against toe-out.

name: Banded Lateral Lunge
cues: Band above the knees, step wide to one side, feet pointing forward
Sit the hips back over the stepping leg, other leg long
Push back to the middle and stand tall
mistakes: Rounding the back to go deeper
regression: Smaller step, hands on a chair
progression: Hold a light kettlebell at the chest
source: Frontal-plane hip strength and adductor length; feet straight works hip rotation control.

name: Single-Arm Band Row with Anti-Rotation
cues: Split stance, anchor at chest height, opposite foot forward
Row one arm, hips and chest stay square to the door
Pause, then return slowly
mistakes: Twisting the trunk to finish the row
Shoulder rolling forward at the end
progression: Half-kneeling or heavier band
youtube: E3 Rehab single arm band row
Eric Cressey half kneeling single arm row
source: Unilateral pulling with an anti-rotation trunk demand; no trunk twist so it stays inside the no-loaded-rotation rule.

name: Banded Glute Bridge March
cues: Band above the knees, bridge up, ribs down
Lift one foot a few centimetres, pelvis stays level
Swap feet slowly, knees pressed out
mistakes: Hips dropping on the lifted side
Pushing the hips so high the low back arches
progression: Hold each lift 5 sec or feet further away
youtube: The Prehab Guys bridge march band
source: Single-leg glute demand with anti-rotation; bridge height stops at a straight line from knee to shoulder (no lumbar extension).

name: Doorway Lat Stretch
cues: Hold the doorframe at head height with one hand
Step back and sit the hips away, arm long
Breathe into the side ribs, spine long
mistakes: Rounding the low back to sink deeper
regression: Arm lower on the frame, smaller range
progression: Hold 45 sec with a slow exhale
youtube: The Prehab Guys lat stretch doorway
source: Tight lats pull the pelvis into tilt and limit overhead range (Janda upper-crossed model); static stretch 30 s per Bandy 1997.

name: Supine Strap Hamstring Stretch
cues: Lie on your back, strap around the ball of one foot, other knee bent
Raise the leg until a gentle stretch in the back of the thigh
Low back stays relaxed on the floor
mistakes: Pulling so hard the hips lift
Pushing into a nerve tug behind the knee
progression: Other leg straight on the floor
setupCue: On your back, strap on foot
youtube: The Prehab Guys strap hamstring stretch
source: Supine keeps the lumbar spine supported; never seated toe touches (loaded flexion). Stop before any nerve tug.

name: Half-Kneeling Banded Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Band anchored low behind you, looped high around the front of the back-leg hip
Tuck the tail under and squeeze that glute first
Shift forward only until the front of the hip stretches
mistakes: Arching the low back to get further forward
Letting the band pull you into a lean
regression: Existing hip flexor stretch with no band
progression: Reach the same-side arm up while ribs stay down
youtube: E3 Rehab banded hip flexor stretch
Kelly Starrett banded hip flexor distraction
source: The band pulls the femoral head forward while the pelvis is tucked; tuck-first cue keeps it inside the no-lumbar-arch rule.

name: Wall Figure-4 Stretch
cues: Lie on your back near a wall, one foot on the wall, knee bent
Cross the other ankle over that knee
Scoot closer to the wall to deepen, hands free
mistakes: Pulling the knee in with the hands
Lifting the low back off the floor
progression: Gently press the crossed knee away
youtube: Bob and Brad piriformis stretch wall
source: Hands-free figure-4: no pulling into lumbar flexion; one knee only.

name: Cross-Body Piriformis Stretch (single knee)
cues: On your back, one leg long, bend the other knee
Guide that knee toward the opposite shoulder with both hands
Stop at a stretch deep in the buttock
mistakes: Twisting the low back off the floor
regression: Smaller range, keep the foot on the floor
progression: Hold 45 sec
source: Single-knee hip flexion with adduction; the pelvis stays on the floor so the lumbar spine does not twist.

name: Adductor Rock-Back
cues: On hands and knees, one leg straight out to the side, foot flat
Rock the hips back slowly until the inner thigh stretches
Back stays long, stop before it rounds
mistakes: Rounding the low back at the end
regression: Smaller rock, knees on a cushion
progression: Hold the end position 5 sec
youtube: The Prehab Guys adductor rock back
source: Dynamic adductor mobility; range stops before lumbar flexion.

name: Wall Calf Stretch (straight and bent knee)
cues: Hands on the wall, one foot back, heel down, toes pointing straight ahead
Straight knee first, then bend the back knee for the lower calf
Hips forward, trunk tall
progression: Hold 45 sec each version
youtube: The Prehab Guys gastrocnemius soleus stretch
source: Limited dorsiflexion pushes people into a toe-out gait; toes-forward position stretches the calf in neutral.

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobility
cues: Face the wall, foot a hand-width away, toes straight
Drive the knee over the second toe toward the wall
Heel stays down
progression: Foot further away, or hold 3 sec
youtube: E3 Rehab ankle dorsiflexion knee to wall
source: Weight-bearing lunge test position; reliable dorsiflexion measure and drill (Bennell 1998).

name: Standing Strap Quad Stretch
cues: One hand on the wall, strap around the ankle behind you
Tuck the tail under first, knees together
Pull the heel up gently with the strap
progression: Step the standing foot onto a low step
setupCue: Hand on wall, strap on ankle
source: Rectus femoris length with a posterior tilt so the lumbar spine does not arch (APT and extension-intolerant rule).

name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
cues: Sit tall, hold the chair seat with one hand
Tilt the ear toward the other shoulder
Let the held shoulder sink
mistakes: Turning the head instead of tilting
progression: Light hand on the head for overpressure
youtube: The Prehab Guys upper trap stretch
source: Desk workers commonly report upper-trap tension; gentle static stretch, never forceful (Cagnie 2007 office workers).

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
cues: Sit tall, hold the chair seat with one hand
Turn the nose toward the other armpit and nod down
Let the held shoulder sink
progression: Light hand on the back of the head
youtube: The Prehab Guys levator scapulae stretch
source: Neck flexion here is unloaded cervical, not lumbar; gentle only. Stop with arm symptoms or dizziness.

name: Child's Pose with Side Reach
cues: Kneel, sit back toward the heels, arms forward
Walk both hands to one side to stretch the opposite flank
Slow breaths into the stretched ribs
mistakes: Forcing the hips down to the heels
regression: Pillow on the calves, smaller sit-back
progression: Hold 45 sec
youtube: The Prehab Guys childs pose side bend
source: Flexion-biased unloaded relief for an extension-intolerant back; contra flexion-intolerant. Unloaded, so allowed by the safety layer.

name: Desk Wrist Flexor Stretch
cues: Arm straight in front, palm up
Gently pull the fingers back with the other hand
Shoulder relaxed
progression: Palm flat on the desk, fingers toward you
source: Forearm flexor length for keyboard and mouse use; stop with tingling (nerve, not muscle).

name: Desk Wrist Extensor Stretch
cues: Arm straight in front, palm down
Bend the wrist down and gently press the back of the hand
Shoulder relaxed
mistakes: Pulling into pain at the elbow
progression: Make a loose fist inside the stretch
youtube: The Prehab Guys tennis elbow stretch
source: Extensor stretch for mouse-heavy work (lateral elbow load); gentle, pain-free.

name: Seated Hip IR Isometric (wall or chair leg)
cues: Sit side-on to the wall, knees at a right angle
Outside of the near foot against the wall
Push the foot into the wall without moving, thigh still
mistakes: Pushing with the whole leg instead of turning the hip
progression: Push harder or hold in more rotation
youtube: E3 Rehab hip internal rotation isometric
The Prehab Guys hip IR isometric
source: Isometrics build strength in end range with low irritability (Rio 2015 on isometric dosing); first rung of the IR ladder.

name: Seated Banded Hip IR (slow lower)
cues: Long band tied to a table leg, looped around the ankle from the inside
Thigh pinned, swing the shin outward
Take 3 seconds to return
progression: Heavier band, hold 3 sec at end range
youtube: E3 Rehab seated hip internal rotation band
source: Eccentric emphasis for the IR muscles; progression from the mini-band version.

name: Side-Lying Hip IR Lift
cues: Lie on your side, knees bent and stacked, pillow between the knees
Keep the top knee down on the pillow
Lift the top foot toward the ceiling, then lower
mistakes: Lifting the knee with the foot
progression: Ankle weight or pause 3 sec at the top
youtube: The Prehab Guys side lying hip internal rotation
source: Open-chain IR strength with gravity resistance; gluteus medius anterior fibres and adductors (Delp 1999 moment arms).

name: Quadruped Hip IR Rock
cues: On hands and knees, knees together, feet wide apart
Rock the hips back slowly, feet staying wide
Stop before the low back rounds
mistakes: Rounding the back at the end
progression: Hold the end 5 sec, one side at a time
youtube: E3 Rehab quadruped hip internal rotation
source: Gentle loaded-position IR mobility; range limited before lumbar flexion.

name: Supported Hip Airplane
cues: Hold a chair, stand on one leg, hinge forward with a flat back
Turn the pelvis open toward the ceiling, then close it toward the floor
The standing knee stays pointing forward
mistakes: Twisting the shoulders instead of the pelvis
regression: Smaller turn, both hands on the chair
progression: One fingertip on the chair, then no support
youtube: The Prehab Guys hip airplane progression
source: Closed-chain IR and ER control on the stance hip; spine stays still, the pelvis rotates over the femur (no lumbar rotation).

name: 90/90 IR Isometric Press
cues: Sit in 90/90, hands behind you for support
Press the back shin and ankle down into the floor
Breathe, trunk tall, no lean
mistakes: Leaning away from the back leg
regression: Prop the hips on a cushion
progression: 90/90 lift-offs (existing ir9090liftoff)
youtube: E3 Rehab 90 90 internal rotation lift off
source: Regression to the lift-off: isometric drive at the same end range (allowed while the lift-off is gated off at Priority).

name: Toe-Forward Glute Bridge
cues: Feet hip-width, toes pointing straight or slightly in
Press through the big toe and heel, knees over the second toe
Lift to a straight line, ribs down
progression: Single-leg bridge or block squeeze
youtube: The Prehab Guys glute bridge foot position
source: Foot position biases hip rotation; toes forward stops turned-out feet driving the bridge with external rotators only.

name: Short Foot (foot tripod)
cues: Stand or sit, weight on heel, big-toe ball and little-toe ball
Draw the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling the toes
The arch lifts, toes stay long
mistakes: Rolling onto the outside of the foot
progression: Single-leg balance holding the tripod
youtube: The Prehab Guys short foot exercise
source: Intrinsic foot strength improves arch control (McKeon 2015 foot core); a stable tripod helps the hip hold neutral rotation.

name: Straight-Foot Walking Drill
cues: Walk along a floor line, feet landing either side pointing forward
Push off through the big toe
Squeeze the back-leg glute as it passes behind
progression: Add a light carry once it feels natural
source: A practice cue, not a correction of structure: normal foot progression angle is roughly 5 to 13 degrees out (Seber 1981); only nudge toward the low end.

name: Chair-Edge Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Sit sideways on the chair edge, one leg back, knee toward the floor
Tuck the tail under, squeeze that glute
Sit tall, feel the front of the hip
mistakes: Arching the back to get more stretch
progression: Reach the same-side arm up, ribs down
youtube: The Prehab Guys seated hip flexor stretch
source: Hip flexor length without getting on the floor; tuck-first keeps it free of lumbar extension.

name: Seated Figure-4 Glute Stretch
cues: Sit tall, ankle on the opposite knee
Hinge forward from the hips with a long back
Stop at a stretch in the buttock
mistakes: Rounding the back to go lower
progression: Gentle hand press on the knee
youtube: Bob and Brad seated piriformis stretch
source: Seated piriformis stretch; hinge from the hips with a neutral spine (no slump).

name: Desk Push-Away Thoracic Stretch
cues: Hands on the desk edge, walk the feet back
Hinge at the hips, let the chest sink between the arms
Ribs stay tucked, breathe out
progression: Hold 5 sec at the bottom
youtube: The Prehab Guys thoracic extension stretch
source: Thoracic extension and shoulder flexion with ribs tucked so the movement stays in the upper back, not the lumbar spine.

name: Chin Tuck with Lean-Back
cues: Sit tall away from the chair back, chin tucked
Lean the trunk back a little, hips as the hinge
Keep the tuck as the head gets heavier
progression: Lean back further or hold 10 sec
youtube: The Prehab Guys chin tuck progression
source: Progresses the deep neck flexor load by changing head angle to gravity (Jull 2008 craniocervical flexion training).

name: Seated Goalpost Slide
cues: Sit back against the chair, arms in a goalpost
Slide the arms up a little and draw them down into the back pockets
Ribs down, chin tucked
progression: Hold 3 sec at the bottom
youtube: The Prehab Guys seated wall slide
source: Desk version of the wall slide; lower-trap emphasis with the chair back as feedback.

name: Standing Hip Extension Squeeze
cues: Stand holding the desk, slight tuck
Take one straight leg a little behind you by squeezing the glute
Stop before the low back moves
mistakes: Swinging the leg high and arching
regression: Glute squeeze only, both feet down
progression: Mini-band around the ankles
youtube: The Prehab Guys standing hip extension
source: Wakes up the glute after sitting; small range so the lumbar spine never extends.

name: Desk Calf Raise
cues: Stand tall, fingertips on the desk
Rise onto the big-toe side of the foot, pause, lower slowly
Ankles stay straight, not rolling out
progression: Single-leg, or 3-sec lowering
source: The calf muscle pump helps return blood after sitting; big-toe bias trains the foot tripod.

name: Median Nerve Slider (gentle)
cues: Arm out to the side, palm up, elbow slightly bent
Bend the wrist back as you tilt the head toward that arm
Then wrist up as the head tilts away
progression: Straighter elbow
youtube: The Prehab Guys median nerve slider
source: Sliders move the nerve without tensioning it (Coppieters 2008). Stop and see a clinician with lasting arm symptoms.

name: Eye and Neck Micro-Break
cues: Look at something far away for 20 seconds
Slow chin tuck, then turn the head gently each way
Three slow breaths, shoulders down
progression: Add a doorway chest stretch
source: The 20-20-20 habit and frequent movement breaks reduce visual and neck discomfort in screen workers (consensus; low-certainty evidence).

name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
cues: Roller across the mid back, below the shoulder blades, hips on the floor
Hands support the head, ribs pulled down
Extend over the roller, then move it up one notch
mistakes: Rolling down onto the low back
regression: Smaller range, roller at one level only
progression: Arms crossed overhead holding a towel
youtube: The Prehab Guys foam roller thoracic extension
E3 Rehab thoracic extension foam roller
source: Thoracic-only extension: hips stay down and the roller never goes below the ribcage, so the lumbar spine stays neutral (load counted as none for the lumbar spine).

name: Foam Roller Quads
cues: Forearm plank, roller under one thigh
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Roll slowly from above the knee to below the hip
mistakes: Low back sagging into an arch
regression: Seated: roll the thigh with your hands
progression: Bend the knee while on a tender spot
youtube: The Prehab Guys quad foam roll
source: Short-term range gain after rolling (Wiewelhove 2019 meta-analysis). Face-down, so plank position must hold; sag is the extension risk.

name: Foam Roller Lats
cues: Lie on your side, roller under the armpit, thumb up
Roll slowly down the side of the ribs
Pause on tender spots and breathe
progression: Reach the arm further overhead
youtube: The Prehab Guys lat foam roll
source: Self-massage for range before overhead or pulling work; short-term effect only.

name: Foam Roller Chest Opener
cues: Lie along the roller, head and tailbone supported, knees bent
Arms out wide, palms up
Let the chest open, low back relaxed
progression: Slow snow angels on the roller
youtube: The Prehab Guys foam roller chest stretch
source: Passive pec stretch in supine; knees bent keep the lumbar spine flat.

name: Massage Ball Glute Release (wall)
cues: Stand with the ball between the buttock and a wall
Lean in and make small circles
Pause on a tender spot and breathe
mistakes: Pressing on a spot that sends pain down the leg
progression: Floor version, or cross the ankle over the knee
setupCue: Ball on buttock, lean on wall
youtube: The Prehab Guys glute lacrosse ball
Bob and Brad piriformis massage ball
source: Standing at a wall keeps it upright and easy to back off; stop if it refers into the leg.

name: Massage Ball Pec Release
cues: Ball just below the collarbone, toward the shoulder
Lean into a wall or doorframe
Slowly move the arm in small circles
mistakes: Pressing into the armpit or on the collarbone
progression: Add arm sweeps overhead
youtube: The Prehab Guys pec minor lacrosse ball
source: Pec minor soft-tissue work before pull-aparts; avoid the armpit (nerves and vessels).

name: Massage Ball Foot Roll
cues: Sit or stand, ball under the arch
Roll slowly from heel to the ball of the foot
Light to moderate pressure
progression: Standing with more weight
youtube: The Prehab Guys plantar fascia massage ball
source: Plantar soft-tissue prep before short-foot work; short-term comfort effect.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift from Blocks
cues: Kettlebell on blocks between the feet, handle at shin height
Hips back, long flat back, brace, then grip
Stand by pushing the floor away and squeezing the glutes, stop tall
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the bell
regression: Higher blocks or band hip hinge
progression: Lower blocks, then heavier bell
source: Raised start keeps the spine neutral for a disc history (McGill hip-hinge rationale). Only at Strengthen or Integrate, pain under 3/10 and no flare.

name: Goblet Box Squat
cues: Hold the bell at your chest, chair behind you
Sit back and down to touch the chair, trunk long
Stand up through the whole foot, knees over toes
progression: Lower box or 3-sec lowering
source: Front-loaded squat keeps the trunk upright; the box sets a depth before the pelvis tucks under.

name: Farmer Carry
cues: A bell in each hand, stand tall, shoulders down
Walk with short steps, toes pointing forward
Ribs over pelvis, breathe
progression: Heavier bells or longer walks
source: Loaded carries train trunk stiffness in upright posture (McGill 2009 carry EMG). Strengthen or Integrate only, no flare.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
cues: Lie face down on an incline bench, chest supported
Row both dumbbells, blades back and down
Lower with control
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
progression: Heavier, or hold 2 sec at the top
source: Bench support removes the bent-over spinal load of free rows (preferred for a disc history).

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
cues: A dumbbell in each hand, long split stance
Lower straight down, trunk tall
Drive through the front heel
progression: Heavier, or rear foot on a low step
source: Unilateral strength with arm-hung load (low spinal moment).

name: Stability Ball Dead Bug
cues: On your back, ball squeezed between hands and knees
Keep squeezing as one arm and the opposite leg reach long
Low back gently into the floor
regression: Squeeze the ball with no limb movement
progression: Same-side arm and leg, or slower
youtube: The Prehab Guys stability ball dead bug
source: Ball squeeze adds anterior-core co-contraction to the dead bug (anti-extension).

name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
cues: On your back, heels on the ball, lift into a bridge
Curl the ball in with the heels, hips stay up
Roll it out slowly
mistakes: Hips dropping as the ball rolls out
Arching the low back to stay up
regression: Bridge hold with heels on the ball
progression: Single-leg curl
youtube: Squat University stability ball hamstring curl
source: Knee-flexion hamstring strength with a neutral bridge (hips to a straight line, never higher).

name: Kneeling Ab Wheel Rollout (short range)
cues: Kneel, wheel under the shoulders, ribs down, glutes squeezed
Roll out only a short way, to a wall stop
Pull back with the arms, no hip pike
mistakes: Low back sagging into an arch at the far end
Hips piking first on the way back
regression: Stability ball rollout on the forearms
progression: Longer range toward the wall stop
source: Contra extension-intolerant on purpose: very high anterior-core demand, and as soon as it fails the lumbar spine sags into loaded extension (Escamilla 2006 rollout EMG). Excluded for this profile.

name: Eccentric Step-Down
cues: Stand on a step, other foot hanging off the front
Take 3 seconds to lower the heel toward the floor
Knee tracks over the second toe, pelvis level
mistakes: Hip dropping on the free side
regression: Lower step, hand on the wall
progression: Higher step or a light dumbbell
youtube: The Prehab Guys lateral step down
source: Frontal-plane knee and hip control (gluteus medius); the eccentric phase drives strength.

name: Slider Hamstring Curl
cues: On your back, heels on sliders, bridge up
Slide the heels out slowly, hips stay up
Pull them back in
regression: Eccentric only: slide out, lower the hips, reset
progression: Single-leg
source: Eccentric hamstring loading; bridge stays at a straight line to protect the lumbar spine.

name: Supported Dead Hang
cues: Grip the bar, feet on a step or the floor taking some weight
Let the shoulders rise toward the ears, breathe slowly
Step down slowly, never drop
mistakes: Dropping off the bar onto the heels
